proposed_widenings.name: shared_item_resource_across_composite_parts
proposed_widenings.justification: The item needs one 20-charge pool shared by its spellcasting branch and its Retributive Strike branch. The current composite magic-item shape gives each activation part its own resource, so encoding both branches would duplicate state.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This staff has 20 charges ... While holding the staff, you can cast one of the spells ... Retributive Strike ... damage equal to 16 times the number of charges in the staff.

proposed_widenings.name: dice_amount_current_resource_pool
proposed_widenings.justification: Retributive Strike damage depends on the number of charges currently remaining in the staff, not a fixed amount, upcast tier, or player-chosen spend.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you take Force damage equal to 16 times the number of charges in the staff. Each other creature in the area ... takes Force damage equal to 4 times the number of charges in the staff.

proposed_widenings.name: item_destruction_on_named_activation
proposed_widenings.justification: The staff is destroyed by taking a specific activation, not by emptying the pool or failing a last-charge roll.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can take a Magic action to break the staff ... The staff is destroyed

proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_numeric_spell_attack_filter
proposed_widenings.justification: The held +2 attack bonus applies to spell attack rolls only. The current surface can filter weapon attacks by weapon, but not distinguish spell attacks from other attack rolls.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While holding it, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class, saving throws, and spell attack rolls.

proposed_widenings.name: probability_gate
proposed_widenings.justification: Retributive Strike has a 50 percent self-avoidance branch before exile/damage resolution. The current surface has no chance-based resolution node.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You have a 50 percent chance to instantly travel to a random plane of existence, avoiding the explosion.

proposed_widenings.name: partial_magic_item_property_loss
proposed_widenings.justification: On last-charge failure the item keeps its weapon bonuses but loses its other properties, which is neither full destruction nor unchanged state.
proposed_widenings.evidence: On a 1, the staff retains its +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls but loses all other properties.
